newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian debt futures ease, no word from RBA.
newsitem.headline: Australian debt futures ease, no word from RBA.

text.p: *Australian debt futures eased slightly after the Reserve Bank made no announcement on monetary policy, a move some had expected in the light of this week's benign inflation data.
*June motor registrations due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian debt futures eased slightly after the Reserve Bank made no announcement on policy, a move some had expected in the light of this week's data

September bill futures touched a low of 94.94 shortly after 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) when policy announcements are usually made, although even at this level it still equates to a cash rate of 5.06 percent compared to official 5.5 percent interest rates.

"(The RBA) has got the numbers to justify the cut. I suspect they are maybe doing some fine tuning on timing, or perhaps just to have the authority of a very recent board meeting behind the decision," said David Lansley, senior econmist at NAB.
The next RBA board meeting is on August 5.
This week's benign outcomes on inflation and wages are seen justifying a rate cut given the economy has yet to see all sectors growing in tandem and with unemployment still high.

Ten-year bond futures also softened after Thursday's rally to an all-ime high of 93.640, and while some analysts see room for the rally to continue a bit further, others see this as the very last stage of a near 200 basis point move since April.
"This is about as good as it gets and we are advising clients to that effect, and it's a market you might want to start selling and take some profits," NAB's Lansley added.

The market unwound some of Thursday's spread tightening to the dollar bloc. The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread made a strong test of 25 basis points on Thursday, its lowest level since the early 1980s. New Zealand bonds continue to strengthen with the N.Z. TWI.
